title: Worker report lands outside the worktree root when the worker changes directory
description:
Found while cleaning up tick is0 (2026-08-20). is0 collected as `missing-result` and blocked cleanup as unexpected dirt. Its report existed and was complete — at `cloud/factory/RESULT-is0.md` rather than the worktree root, because the worker had cdd into that package and wrote the file relative to its cwd.

Two consequences, both real:
1. collect looks only at the worktree root, so a complete report reads as no report — and the orchestrator nearly discarded a report containing a genuine unproven risk (only `content` was translated for the Workers AI route; omp also sends `store`, `stream_options` and `max_completion_tokens`, which the route evidently tolerates but which nothing has proved).
2. cleanup refuses the worktree because the stray file is dirt it does not recognise, which is how a closed tick kept its worker alive.

The prompt template already says "at the root of this worktree", so this is not a missing instruction — it is an instruction that a worker following it from a subdirectory gets wrong. Prefer a mechanism over more prose: have collect look for RESULT-<tick>.md anywhere in the worktree and say where it found it when that is not the root, and/or have the prompt give the absolute path rather than a relative one.
acceptance_criteria: A report written from a subdirectory is found by collect, with its location named when it is not the root; cleanup is not blocked by it; the prompt template gives an unambiguous path.
